prompt: Why do speech systems take the logarithm of spectrogram energies?
options: to compress a huge dynamic range, matching how loudness is perceived
explanation: Energies span many orders of magnitude and loudness is perceived roughly logarithmically; the log also turns products into sums.

prompt: Using $m=2595\log_{10}(1+f/700)$, what is the mel value of 700 Hz? (Give a number rounded to the nearest integer.)
A mel filterbank has 80 filters and the FFT has 400 points (201 one-sided bins). What is the shape of the filterbank matrix $\mathbf H$?
explanation: One row per filter and one column per one-sided FFT bin: $(M, N/2+1)=(80,201)$; the mel spectrogram is $\mathbf P\mathbf H^\top$.

prompt: Mel filters are equally spaced on the mel axis. In hertz, the filters are...
options: all the same height and width in bins
explanation: The mel axis compresses high frequencies, so equal mel steps are larger and larger in hertz.

prompt: You compute 13 MFCCs, 13 deltas and 13 delta-deltas per frame. How many features per frame?
What is the role of the DCT in MFCC computation?
options: it rotates the log-mel vector into a basis where the first coefficients hold the smooth spectral outline
it measures how fast the features change
explanation: The orthonormal DCT-II re-expresses the log-mel vector as slow to fast cosines; truncating keeps the envelope.

prompt: The orthonormal DCT-II matrix $\mathbf D$ satisfies...
explanation: Rows are orthonormal, so $\mathbf D$ is a rotation and the inverse transform is $\mathbf D^\top$.

prompt: The delta of a feature sequence that increases by exactly 2 per frame (in the interior) is...
explanation: The delta formula is the least-squares slope in feature units per frame; for a perfect line it is the slope, 2.

prompt: What is $dm/df$ in mel per Hz at $f=0$ (to two decimals)? Use $2595/(700\ln 10)$.
explanation: $2595/(700\cdot2.3026)=1.61$; it falls to 0.66 at 1 kHz and 0.13 at 8 kHz.
